It contains a high-energy thioester bond, not a phosphate bond. Coenzyme A, a component of Acetyl-CoA, includes an adenine nucleotide, not a guanine nucleotide. Acetyl-CoA plays a regulatory role by activating pyruvate carboxylase and inhibiting pyruvate dehydrogenase, which is consistent with its function in metabolic pathways. It does not easily cross the mitochondrial inner membrane and requires conversion to citrate for transport.
